plan.title: UC inflamed vs control: hallmark pathway activity heatmap
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is a per-sample pathway activity score and a hallmark heatmap separating UC-inflamed colon from control colon (6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch, Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes). The knowledge service's full_plan procedure for this exact situation (2 groups, 6/6, unpaired, no batch, low-depth-sample flag, pathway_activity+signature_scoring requested with sample_scores enrichment input) is followed and was checked with execute_knowledge_check (ok:true, no violations). Sequence: (1) sample-structure QC that surfaces sample_01's low depth without silently dropping it; (2) minimal count filter and DESeq2 normalization/model with an explicit reference level (control) and named contrast (condition inflamed vs control); (3) DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, BH/independent filtering — this both answers a companion DE question and supplies the Wald statistic used later as a ranking metric; (4) the core deliverable: GSVA per-sample Hallmark (MSigDB 2026.1, 50 sets) activity scores on variance-stabilized expression, giving one score per sample per pathway, tested between conditions with limma and visualized as a ComplexHeatmap of samples x hallmark pathways annotated by condition and by library-size/QC flag; (5) decoupleR mlm on the PROGENy footprint model as a second, complementary pathway-activity view (14 signalling pathways, footprint-based, not membership-based) on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, cross-referenced against the GSVA hallmark result; (6) UCell signature scores as the additional per-sample scoring requested, for robustness/triangulation; (7) a single report step assembling QC diagnostics, DE summary, both pathway-activity views, and the annotated heatmap with full reproducibility record. All reference collections (MSigDB Hallmark human 2026.1, PROGENy human weights) and packages (DESeq2, apeglm, GSVA, decoupleR/Python, limma, ComplexHeatmap, UCell) are confirmed present in this environment.
